aarti.pad1: I bow to the Lord of the Raghus, the treasury of compassion,
through whom the worldly knowledge that sees difference falls away.
aarti.pad2: He is the moon that gladdens the night-lilies of Raghu's line;
Brahmā and Śiva serve his lotus feet.
aarti.pad3: He is the bee in the lotus of his own devotees' hearts;
his lovely form is like countless gods of love.
aarti.pad4: He is the sun to the overpowering darkness of delusion,
and a fierce fire to the dense forest of ignorance.
aarti.pad5: He is the pot-born Agastya to the ocean of pride, and generous;
he delights the gods and breaks the burden of the earth.
aarti.pad6: He is Garuḍa to the swarms of serpents that are attachment and the rest,
a lion to the elephant of Kāma, and Murāri, the foe of Mura.
aarti.pad7: His lotus feet are the ship across the ocean of worldly existence;
he is Jānakī's beloved, the root of bliss.
aarti.pad8: He is the swan in the pool of Hanumān's love,
the wish-granting cow to those who are free of desire, and compassionate.
aarti.pad9: Rāma, the ornament of the three worlds and fathomless in virtue,
is the abode of rest, says Tulasīdāsa.
